s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Few yellow spots on fundus examination
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence
OCT shows inner retinal thickening and disorganization
Complete loss of photoreceptors in superotemporal region

shortlist.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and fundus examination findings are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects, along with fundus autofluorescence and OCT findings, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Gyrate atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms and findings to retinitis pigmentosa, with the addition of a possible link to ornithine aminotransferase deficiency

shortlist.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically presenting in infancy, some forms may have a later onset, and the patient's night blindness since childhood warrants consideration of this rare diagnosis

shortlist.label: Rod-cone dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic findings, including the abnormal electroretinogram and fundus examination, are consistent with this diagnosis, which is a broader category that may encompass some of the other differentials

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and fundus autofluorescence showing hypofluorescence are consistent with rod-cone dystrophy. The presence of few yellow spots on fundus examination and inner retinal thickening on OCT also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: While retinitis pigmentosa can cause night blindness, the fundus examination in this case does not show typical pigmentary degeneration.

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Choroideremia typically affects males and causes more severe visual impairment, which is not consistent with this patient's visual acuity of 20/25 to 20/30.

rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
rejected.why: Gyrate atrophy is associated with ornithine aminotransferase deficiency and typically causes more extensive chorioretinal atrophy, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: Leber congenital amaurosis typically presents with severe visual impairment and nystagmus in infancy, which is not consistent with this patient's history and visual acuity.
